prohibited_concomitant: Systemic (oral, intra-venous or intra-muscular), intra-lesional or topical corticosteroids; imiquimod; vincristine; alfa-interferon; propranolol or other beta-blockers were prohibited at any time prior to or during the study.
Beta-blockers, including propranolol, were prohibited for the mother prior to and during the study if she was breastfeeding the infant.
For a breastfeeding mother, systemic corticosteroids, vincristine, and alfa-interferon were prohibited within 14 days of randomization or during the study.
value.population_note: The review lists prohibited concomitant medications and timing; it does not enumerate permitted concomitant medications.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Study 201 concomitant medication restrictions: "TITLE: Protocol # V00400 SB 201:" "The following medications were prohibited for the patient at any time prior to or during the study:" " Systemic (oral, intra-venous or intra-muscular), intra-lesional or topical corticosteroids" " Imiquimod" " Vincristine" " Alfa-interferon" " Propranolol or other beta-blockers" "Beta-blockers (including propranolol) were also prohibited for the mother prior to and during the" "study if she was breastfeeding the infant at the same time." "The following medications were also" "prohibited for the mother within 14 days of randomization or during the study if she was" "breastfeeding the infant:" " Systemic (oral, intra-venous or intra-muscular) corticosteroids" " Vincristine" " Alfa-interferon" -- The FDA clinical review states these restrictions applied before and/or during the study as specified. It does not describe a background regimen or list permitted concomitant medications.

method_citations: Weighted inverse-normal combination test with Simes adjustment for the primary analysis; closed-test gate to the key secondary endpoint at W48

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: FDA Medical Review, Section 9.4.1, Statistical Methods and W48 key secondary analysis: "Statistical Methods: The primary analysis was to test for superiority of the selected regimen(s) of" "propranolol versus placebo." "The p-values from the first and second stages of the study were" "combined using the weighted inverse normal combination function." "Simes’ method was used to" "define an adjusted first stage p-value (and an adjusted second stage p value in the case where" "two regimens were chosen at the interim analysis) to ensure that the type I error rate was" "controlled at less than or equal to a nominal one-sided significance level of 0.005." "For the key secondary efficacy analysis at W48, a combination test computed in the same way" "as the primary endpoint was used to analyze success/failure based on the investigator on-site" "qualitative assessment of complete resolution of the target IH at W48." "If the primary null" "hypothesis was rejected at the one-sided 0.005 significance level, the closed test procedure" "then allowed the key secondary endpoint to be tested on the ITT data set while maintaining the" "overall type I error rate at a nominal one-sided significance level ≤ 0.005." " The primary efficacy criterion was evaluated at Week 24 (or premature discontinuation of" -- The review describes one-sided alpha 0.005, weighted inverse-normal combination tests and Simes adjustment for primary testing, then a closed-test gate that permits the W48 key secondary test only after rejecting the primary null. This supports familywise type-I-error control and an explicit W24-to-W48 gate. The schema procedure enum does not represent this combination-test/Simes method, so procedure is null. The source does not establish that this method was finalized in a SAP, so finalized_in_sap is null. Week numbers are read from the source's W24 and W48 visit labels. The source states the gate order but does not number steps, so the optional step fields remain null.

"‡Calculated on time to first sustained improvement assessed at D0, D7, D14, D21, W5, W8, W12, W16, W20, W24." "The study duration was approximately 13 months for recruitment, 24 weeks of treatment and 72" "weeks follow up (total = 96 week study duration per patient)." value.rationale: During worsening in the study treatment period, if the investigator considered a new treatment necessary for the patient's well-being, a new treatment of the investigator's choice could be administered and study treatment was permanently discontinued.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Study design: new treatment in case of worsening: "In the case of a worsening of IH during the study treatment period for which the investigator" "considered it was necessary for the Patient’s well-being to administer a new treatment of" "his/her choice, the study treatment was permanently discontinued." -- The source permits a new treatment at investigator choice for worsening and requires permanent discontinuation of study treatment.

death_rate.source_excerpt: FDA Medical Review, Sections 7.1 and 7.3.1 and Table 37 pooled safety population with overrun: "Study V00400 SB 2 01 (Study 201 – the pivotal trial)" "The Safety Population is defined as all patients who received at least 1 study treatment." "(1) Frequency of adverse events (AEs) from the pooled database {Study 201 (401" "propranolol/55 placebo) and Study 102 (23 infants)} totaling 424 patients with IH" "Table 37 Extent of exposure: Safety population – pooled (with overrun)" "Extent of Placebo Propranolol Propranolol Propranolol Propranolol Propranolol" "exposure 1 mg/kg/day 1 mg/kg/day 3 mg/kg/day 3 mg/kg/day Total" "(days)* 3mths 6mths 3mths 6mths" "N/missing 55/0 98/0 102/0 100/0 101/0 456/0" "Pooled Safety Population: There were no deaths in the pooled safety population." -- The review maps V00400 SB 201 to Study 201 and identifies Study 201 as part of the pooled safety database (401 propranolol and 55 placebo participants); it defines the safety population as all treated patients. The same review reports no deaths in that pooled safety population. Table 37 gives the pooled safety denominators by Study 201 regimen (55, 98, 102, 100, 101; total 456). The no-deaths statement applies to the pooled population containing this trial; percent is left null rather than calculated.

published_results.source_excerpt: FDA Medical Review, Table 11, Overall (Pooled ITT with overrun) Analysis, primary endpoint at W24: "Study V00400 SB 2 01 (Study 201 – the pivotal trial)" "Study 201 is a randomized, placebo-controlled, multi-dose, 2-stage, adaptive design" "study to select the best of four regimens of propranolol (1 and 3 mg/kg/day, each for 3" "or 6 months, following up-titration) at the end of the first stage in a seamless phase II/III" "Table 11 Similar primary efficacy results for the treatment regimens between" "Stage 1 population (interim analysis) and Pooled with overrun population" "Placebo Propranolol Propranolol Propranolol Propranolol" "1 mg/kg/day 3mths 1 mg/kg/day 6mths 3 mg/kg/day 3mths 3 mg/kg/day 6mths" "n (%) n (%) P-value n (%) P-value n (%) P-value n (%) P-value" "Overall (Pooled ITT with overrun) Analysis" "N 55 98 102 100 101" "Primary endpoint 2 (3.6%) 8 (8.2%) 50 (49.0%) 12 (12.0%) 61 (60.4%)" "of complete/nearly complete resolution of IH at W24 (assessed by central reading of the" -- Table 11 identifies this as the Overall (Pooled ITT with overrun) analysis and prints a distinct row of primary-endpoint results with the five arm denominators. This is the W24 Primary Analysis endpoint (endpoint_keys primary position 2); the separate Stage I interim analysis is not joined here. analysis_population is null because the schema has no value for pooled ITT with overrun. Arm IDs are aligned to the five Table 11 columns and the base trial arm labels.
